_comment: Committed SCORE FLOORS for the labelled sample set. `python -m evals.gate` runs the suites and fails (exit 1) if any metric drops below its floor — so a change that degrades retrieval, routing, citations, or verification is caught before it merges. After a genuine improvement run `--ratchet` to raise these numbers, so the gate gets stricter over time and the agent can't silently regress to yesterday's quality.
_tiers: retrieval.* and trajectory.* are deterministic and free (they run in CI with no API keys). agent.* needs a chat key. judge.correctness is opt-in (--judge) because it spends judge calls; it is deliberately scored by a DIFFERENT model family than the answerer.
_floors_note: Floors come from `--ratchet`: deterministic metrics (retrieval math, structural trajectory checks, the regex router) are held EXACTLY at the observed score; LLM-dependent metrics get a 0.05 variance margin so normal model non-determinism doesn't fail the build — a gate that cries wolf gets ignored. KNOWN GAPS being worked, floors set low deliberately: trajectory.calculator_ran_when_routed (calc-lane questions that don't produce a deterministic computation) and agent.abstain_accuracy (one semantically adjacent out-of-scope question).
